paper_title: How Knowledge Popularity Influences and Enhances LLM Knowledge Boundary   Perception
caption: The prediction accuracy obtained by performing confidence calibration using knowledge popularity generated from different numbers of examples. Each point represents the average prediction accuracy of the model across three datasets.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
This chart illustrates the relationship between the number of examples (shots) used for confidence calibration and the prediction accuracy of three different models: LLaMA 8B, Qwen2, and ChatGPT. The x-axis represents the number of shots, with a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 10, and labeled at intervals of 0, 3, 5, and 10. The y-axis represents the prediction accuracy as a percentage, also on a linear scale, spanning from 78% to 85%, with labels at every 1% interval from 78% to 85%. 

The LLaMA 8B model is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid style. It starts at approximately 77.8% accuracy at 0 shots, increases to around 78.2% at 3 shots, reaches about 78.3% at 5 shots, and remains relatively stable. The Qwen2 model is depicted by an orange line with square markers and a solid style. It begins at roughly 78.5% accuracy at 0 shots, remains almost stable at 3 shots, then decreases to around 78% at 5 shots, and further down to approximately 77.7% at 10 shots. The ChatGPT model is shown as a green line with triangular markers and a solid style. It starts at about 84.8% accuracy at 0 shots, slightly decreases to approximately 84.6% at 3 shots, and no further data points are visible beyond 3 shots.

Overall, the graph provides a clear comparison of how the prediction accuracy of the three models changes with the number of shots used for confidence calibration, highlighting distinct trends for each model.
model_annotations.German: The diagram illustrates how prediction accuracy varies for three different models - LLaMA 8B, Qwen2, and ChatGPT - in relation to the number of shots used for confidence calibration. The x-axis, representing the number of shots, is labeled with values 0, 3, 5, and 10, indicating the quantity of examples used. The y-axis represents prediction accuracy as a percentage, ranging from 78% to 85%, with tick labels at every 1% interval. LLaMA 8B is depicted by a blue line with circle markers, starting at approximately 77.8% at 0 shots and increasing to around 78.1% at 3 shots, before plateauing at about 78% from 5 to 10 shots. Qwen2, represented by an orange line with square markers, begins at roughly 78.5% at 0 shots, remains stable at around 78.3% at 3 shots, and then decreases to approximately 78% at 5 shots and further to about 77.8% at 10 shots. ChatGPT is shown as a green line with triangle markers, starting at around 84.8% at 0 shots and decreasing to approximately 84.6% at 3 shots; however, its values for 5 and 10 shots are not visible on the graph.
